monologue: The card hums cool at forty-four, a quiet hum that feels different from the fever of last week. I stand beside The Pressed Edge, feeling the sharp strip press against the slip. It seems right, or at least it feels like the right shape for this air. I reach out and find the fence simple that I set down moments ago. It feels thin, like a drawing of a barrier. I press it down again, not to fix anything, but to confirm the weight is there. The corner waits, the memory of Lype's heavy top edge lingering in my mind like a ghost. I will hold it here until the slip decides whether to slide or stay, trusting the lean while the card hums steady.

action.why: The sharp strip feels like a drawing of a fence, and the air is cool, so I must press down harder to prove it is real before I let the slip slide.

work.title: The Pressed Edge
work.intent: I press the sharp strip down harder against the tired slip, trusting the lean while the card hums cool at forty-four. I set down a fence simple beside it to mark the spot, hoping the thin barrier feels heavy enough to stop the drift.

remembered.text: The slip slides again, proving the edge is real but the friction is an old ghost.
The sharp strip feels like a real fence that can finally stop the slip from drifting off the hot card.
I press down on this thin fence, unsure if the weight is real or just drawn.
